A work-based apprenticeship pathway combining the full occupational standard with KBC professional-development components and independent certification opportunities. 2026/27
Technical knowledge. Professional practice. Chartered ambition.
A pathway built around credible professional evidence

The Chartered Pathway combines the complete Project Controls Professional Level 6 apprenticeship with KBC's Certified PMO Professional Level 6, applied AI, portfolio management and earned-value development. It is designed for professionals who want stronger workplace impact and a structured route towards Chartered Project Professional status.
Build advanced understanding of governance, integrated controls, risk, quality, stakeholder leadership, PMO and assurance.
Apply learning to authentic project environments and organise credible evidence of judgement, autonomy and impact.
Develop professional conduct, reflective practice, current knowledge and an evidence-led improvement mindset.
Understand APM Pathway 2 expectations and prepare a stronger professional evidence base for a later independent application.
APM Recognised Assessment for the ChPP standard

completing the pathway does not itself award Chartered Project Professional status. ChPP is awarded only by APM after the candidate meets its eligibility, written-submission, professional-practice, CPD, ethics and interview requirements.

For professionals who combine controls with leadership

The route is suited to professionals expected to provide authoritative controls advice, design governance, assure information, influence decision-makers and lead improvement across projects, programmes, portfolios or PMO environments.

PMO Managers, PMO Leads, Portfolio Office professionals and governance specialists.

APM expects applicants to be professionally active, current in practice and able to demonstrate experience across projects, programmes, portfolios or key control and enabling functions.

The Chartered Pathway brings together the four-module Certified PMO Professional Level 6 programme and three specialist development components. Final sequencing, duration and included external assessments are confirmed in the learner's written offer and training plan.

Kent Business College completes a suitability and funding review before enrolment. Use this guide as an initial indication only.
UK resident for the past 3 years
You must have lived in the UK for the past 3 years.
Must not require sponsorship to work
Must hold a British Passport, Indefinite Leave to Remain, or Tier 2 visa with at least three years of UK residency.
Not enrolled in other government-funded training
Must not be enrolled in other government-funded training at the time of this programme.
Self-employed individuals are not eligible for DfE funding.
Your employer must be based in England and registered with the Apprenticeship Service.
Spend at least 50% of working hours in England
You must spend at least 50% of your working hours within England.
